rationale: Tests recall of the precise legal definition distinguishing poison from drug — a foundational distinction for medico-legal reporting.
Tests understanding of which Indian statute specifically governs the sale of scheduled poisons through licensed vendors — a common exam and practical-skills question.
Tests classification knowledge — distinguishing organophosphates (organic synthetic origin) from animal, mineral, and gaseous categories.
Addresses a common toxicokinetics misconception about volume of distribution: high Vd means extensive tissue uptake and LOW blood levels, not high blood levels.
Tests the critical contraindication list for activated charcoal — iron is an absolute contraindication because charcoal does not adsorb inorganic ions.
Tests the time-window rule for pralidoxime (PAM) in organophosphate poisoning — PAM loses effectiveness after AChE 'ageing' at 24–48 hours.
Tests knowledge of the pathognomonic post-mortem finding in CO poisoning — cherry-pink lividity from carboxyhaemoglobin.
Tests the absolute contraindication of formalin for toxicological viscera specimens — formalin destroys organic poison residues and invalidates FSL chemical analysis.
Tests knowledge of the ferric chloride bedside urine test — purple colour indicates paracetamol or salicylate, a rapid point-of-care test.
Tests understanding that AAS is specific to metallic elements only — it cannot detect organic compounds, which require chromatographic methods.
Tests understanding of mesothelioma's unusually long latency period — the 20–50 year gap between asbestos exposure and disease onset creates severe medicolegal challenges.
Tests recall of the chronic arsenicosis clinical triad — raindrop pigmentation, palmoplantar keratosis, and Mees' lines from groundwater arsenic in West Bengal.
